desc:
Cloud hosting setup for your app gives your product a secure, reliable home in an account you own. Ecom Swift LLC builds the servers or services, database, storage, firewall, HTTPS and alerts on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, DigitalOcean or a simpler host.

## What is cloud hosting setup?

Cloud hosting setup is the work of preparing a place in the cloud where your app runs and your data lives. It covers the server or container service, the database, file storage, the network rules, the certificate and the monitoring. It also covers how new versions of your app get onto it.

Choosing a provider is only the first step. A new cloud account is a blank space, and the defaults are rarely safe or economical. Someone has to decide what to create, how the pieces connect and who can reach them.

## Why the first setup matters

Early decisions are expensive to change later. A database exposed to the internet, a single server with no backup or a tangle of manually created resources can all work for weeks and then fail at a bad time. Rebuilding a live environment while customers are using it is far harder than building it correctly the first time.

Ownership matters as well. If a developer or agency creates the hosting under their own account, you may not control your product. We build in your account, with you as the owner, so the system stays yours whoever works on it next.

## How good hosting affects your product

Hosting shapes everything users feel. A suitable server size keeps pages responsive. A private network keeps the database out of reach. HTTPS protects logins and payments. An uptime check tells you about an outage before a customer does.

It shapes your costs too. A set-up sized for your real traffic avoids paying for a large cluster you do not need, while leaving room to grow. A cost estimate at the end of the work helps you plan, and written notes mean the next engineer does not start from zero.

## What a sound cloud set-up includes

- A server, container service or managed app platform matched to your size and skills.
- A database, either managed by the provider or installed with care, with daily backups.
- File storage for uploads and media, kept apart from the app server.
- A private network so the database is not open to the public internet.
- A firewall that allows only the traffic your app needs.
- HTTPS with a certificate that renews on its own.
- Secrets such as keys and passwords kept in a protected store, not in code.
- An uptime check and an alert to a person who can act on it.
- A repeatable way to deploy updates, such as a script or pipeline.
- A simple diagram and notes describing what exists and why.

## How we build it

We begin with a short conversation about your app, your expected traffic and your team. From that we recommend a provider and an architecture, explaining the trade-offs in plain terms. You may prefer a simple platform that hides most of the work, or a more flexible cloud service where you control each piece.

We then create the resources in your account, connect them, deploy your app and test it end to end. In the larger package we write the infrastructure as code, so the whole set-up can be recreated or reviewed from a file. Basic covers a single secure server. Standard adds the database, storage and monitoring. Premium adds load balancing, a managed database, a CDN and a handover call. You pay the cloud provider directly for the running costs.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Create the cloud account yourself, in your own name or company name.
- Turn on two-factor sign-in for every administrator.
- Keep production and test environments separate.
- Write down what each resource is for.
- Set a budget alert on day one.

**Avoid:**
- Letting a contractor own the account that runs your product.
- Putting the database on a public address.
- Using one shared administrator login.
- Sizing for a traffic spike that may never arrive.
- Deploying by hand with no record of what changed.

## Who this is for

This service suits a founder whose app runs only on a developer's laptop or a shared host and who needs a proper home. It suits a small agency that wants a standard, secure base for client projects. It also suits a business moving off a provider it has outgrown.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of your app, its language or framework, where the code is kept and any traffic you expect. We never need your passwords. If you already have a cloud account, add us as a limited collaborator or team user. If you do not, we guide you through creating one so you remain the owner.
